clue.text: Impetus given by financial set-up covering hotel

indicators.note: covering says the financial arrangement wraps round the hotel letter

parts.note: a trust is a financial arrangement holding assets for others
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Economic momentum comes from an investment fund that owns a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a driving force or forward push, as in the thrust of an argument.

clue.text: Wins one in ruff with hearts voided

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one inside the bridge word

parts.note: in bridge to ruff is to trump
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: voided means emptied, leaving only the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A bridge player wins by trumping after running out of hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Victories are triumphs, both nouns for successes.

clue.text: There's no interest initially in new primrose onesies

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into a fresh arrangement once the extra letter is removed
initially takes the first letter of interest

explanation.surface: A fresh flower-coloured baby suit nobody cares about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's no' takes I out of PRIMROSE; 'new' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: One-piece garments for babies or toddlers, the US word for a romper suit.

clue.text: Team on course to create a diversion

parts.note: a side is a team
a race track is a course

explanation.surface: A team on the race circuit makes a feint.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert someone from the main point is to distract them, a verb phrase sense.

clue.text: Especially lovable possibly after answer

indicators.note: after places the scrambled word behind the single letter for answer
possibly signals that the letters of lovable may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Something especially lovable is perhaps judged so after a reply comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Especially' opens the surface as an adverb on lovable but is the definition; 'possibly' scrambles the following word, and answer as A is a standard exam abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means most of all, a close synonym of especially in sentences like 'he wanted, especially, peace'.

clue.text: Study, say, covered by B 'n' B giving livelihood

indicators.note: covered by says each B is placed over the word that follows it, down the column

parts.note: the letter as printed
to read is to study
n is an informal short form of and
the letter as printed
to say is to utter

explanation.surface: Reading at a bed and breakfast brings in a living.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface B 'n' B is a bed and breakfast guesthouse; in the down entry its two letters each sit atop a word, so 'covered by' works vertically.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic income is described as one's staple fare, figuratively a living.

clue.text: Source of illness in Queen Victoria — American bug

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the royal cipher

parts.note: VR, Victoria Regina, was Queen Victoria's royal cipher

indicators.note: source of takes the first letter of the following word

parts.note: US means American

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria caught an American germ.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug is informally a germ or infection.

clue.text: Sin of a vicar going wrong with end of service

indicators.note: going wrong signals a jumbling of the letters of a vicar
end of takes the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A clergyman errs at the close of worship, committing a sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wrong' rearranges AVICAR into AVARIC, then E.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Broadcast 'Smiley's People' (US)

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Airing the spy drama Smiley's People on American television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smiley's People' is a John le Carré spy novel adapted for BBC TV. 'Broadcast' rearranges SMILEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans use the slang term for British people, from sailors given lime juice.

clue.text: Country music?

parts.note: not the musical genre but a song representing a nation

explanation.definitionFit: A song officially adopted by a nation is literally its own music.

clue.text: Urgent note given to press and TV after one married

indicators.note: after puts the press and TV piece behind the one and married letters

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
newspapers and television together are the media
TE is a note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A pressing memo is sent to journalists and broadcasters after someone weds.
explanation.definitionFit: Something urgent needs action at once, which is the sense of the adjective here.

clue.text: Genuine male domain

parts.note: genuine means real

explanation.surface: A true man's territory, the stereotypical masculine preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom or sphere of influence is a domain, synonyms in both literal and figurative use.

clue.text: Mother is French and runs international experts

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
est is French for is
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A mother of French nationality who competes globally is a top performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian plural for masters of an art, especially great conductors or musicians, so skilled experts.

clue.text: Does without love — and small fortune

indicators.note: without says the zero letter for love is removed from the word does

parts.note: love means zero in tennis scoring, written O
small means tiny

explanation.surface: Someone lacking romance ends up with only a modest fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes O out of DOES, leaving DES. 'Fortune' looks like money but means fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune in the sense of fate or what lies in store is a synonym for one's lot in life.

clue.text: Entertainer needing a plant

parts.note: a host entertains guests

explanation.surface: A party-giver requires a houseplant.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy shade-loving garden perennial, also called the plantain lily.

clue.text: More than eight draws gets you a naughty time

parts.note: nine is one more than eight
drawn games are ties

explanation.surface: A gambler with more than eight tied results enjoys a racy spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1890s are known as the 'Naughty Nineties' for their supposed decadence.
explanation.definitionFit: The decade of the 1890s is popularly called naughty, a fixed historical phrase.

clue.text: Ability to resist Spanish cheer in dreamlike state

indicators.note: in puts the cheer inside the dream state

parts.note: a trance is a dreamlike state
olé is a Spanish cry of approval

explanation.surface: Spanish applause can't rouse someone in a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is the capacity to endure, as in tolerance to a drug.

clue.text: Favourite Oxbridge sportsman watched

parts.note: a blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge university at sport
eyed means watched

explanation.surface: A university athlete was being watched as the favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-eyed boy is a pet or darling, so favoured.

clue.text: Society that might make Spooner's chef weep?

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: a chef is a cook
to blub is to weep, a British informal word

explanation.surface: A gathering that might reduce the reverend's chef to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: COOK BLUB with initial letters swapped gives the society; blub is British slang for crying.
explanation.definitionFit: A group meeting regularly to discuss reading is a society of members.

clue.text: Old river tribe lost craft

indicators.note: lost means astray, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: An ancient river people vanished along with their boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft orbiting a planet is an orbiter.

clue.text: Tag left on the first person to be killed

parts.words: the first person to be killed
parts.note: in Genesis Abel is murdered by Cain, the first killing

explanation.surface: A tag was left on the body of the first murder victim.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag and a label are both small tickets attached to identify something.

clue.text: Tennessee woman almost turned white

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to blanch is to go pale, so blanched means turned white

explanation.surface: A Tennessee lady nearly went pale.
explanation.walkthrough: Blanche DuBois is the heroine of Tennessee Williams's A Streetcar Named Desire; 'Tennessee' is the playwright, not the state.
explanation.definitionFit: The most famous character created by playwright Tennessee Williams bears this first name.

clue.text: Computer circuit ranking above all others

parts.note: a lap is a circuit of a track
top means best of all

explanation.surface: A computer race lap at the head of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable personal computer used on the knees is this kind.

clue.text: White gold plating pound pieces

indicators.note: plating says the gold symbol surrounds the pound abbreviation like a coating

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
chess pieces are called men

explanation.surface: Gold coating on coins worth a pound each.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' looks like coins in the surface but means chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: The white of an egg is its albumen, the clear part that turns white when cooked.

clue.text: Value some consumer items

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Certain shopping goods are worth something.
explanation.definitionFit: Worth or excellence; merit is a synonym of value in that sense.

clue.text: Area outside house for caterer to cook

indicators.note: cooking the letters means doctoring or rearranging them

explanation.surface: A patio space where the hired caterer can prepare food.
explanation.definitionFit: A paved patio next to a home is a terrace, a level outdoor area.

clue.text: Coach tour in chaos around west of Torquay

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters sit on either side of the inserted letter
in chaos says the letters of tour are jumbled
in an across entry the west end of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bus trip around a seaside resort falls into disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in chaos' turns TOUR into UTOR; 'around' puts it round T. Torquay is an English seaside resort in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach is to tutor, both meaning to give private instruction.

clue.text: The chase that's on for handy cure to be developed?

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A race is on to develop a convenient remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the outcry raised to pursue a criminal, so a noisy chase or public pursuit.

clue.text: Leave before final whistle, for example, not fully committed

indicators.note: before puts the leave word ahead of the whistle word

parts.note: to part is to leave
the referee's final whistle signals time in football

explanation.surface: Leaving the match early suggests a fan not wholly devoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time!' is called at the end of a match, and the final whistle is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Working fewer than full hours describes someone not fully committed to a job.

clue.text: Top bunk occupied by the man third in class

indicators.note: occupied by says the bed holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a bunk is a bed
he refers to the man

indicators.note: third in takes the third letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A man who sleeps in the upper bunk comes third in the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective but is slang for kill, here by decapitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang top means kill, and removing the head is a literal topping.
